section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to leave the interstate for an exit, you should:
options: a:Be in the proper lane at least one mile before your exit and do not slow until on the deceleration lane.,b:Signal and slow down 50–100 feet before the ramp.,c:Reduce to 45 mph one mile before exiting.,d:Stop in the exit lane before slowing.
note: On freeways, you should plan ahead and move into the correct lane well before your exit so you can safely reach the deceleration lane. Stay at freeway speed until you are actually in the deceleration lane, then slow down there. Slowing early in the through lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: When are roads especially slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:When it has been raining for an hour or more.,b:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,c:The day after it rains.
note: Roads are especially slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm. Oil and residue on the road surface mix with the new rainwater and create a slick film. After it has rained for a while, much of this buildup is washed away and traction usually improves, though you should still drive carefully.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit on a county road without a hard surface is:
options: a:45 miles per hour.,b:55 miles per hour,c:50 miles per hour.,d:40 miles per hour.
note: Speed limits on unpaved or gravel county roads are set by each state and can vary; there is no single standard limit that applies everywhere in the U.S. Always follow the posted speed limit for that specific road, and if no limit is posted, follow your state’s default rural speed limit and adjust your speed for conditions such as loose gravel, dust, and reduced traction.

question: May you use parking lights instead of headlights when driving at night?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You may not drive at night using only parking lights. Parking lights are for when a vehicle is stopped or parked to make it visible, not for driving. When it is dark or visibility is reduced, you must use your headlights so you can see the road and so other drivers can see you.

question: As daylight begins to fade, what should you use to make your vehicle more visible?
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: As daylight fades, turn on your low beam headlights so other drivers can see you and you can see the road clearly. Parking lights and emergency flashers are not a substitute for headlights while driving. Use high beams only on very dark roads when there is no oncoming traffic or vehicle directly ahead of you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: At a four-way stop, the driver on the right should insist on the right-of-way.
options: a:False,b:True
note: At a four‑way stop, the driver on the right generally has the legal right‑of‑way when vehicles arrive at the same time, but no driver should insist on that right if it could lead to a collision. If another driver moves first or seems confused, you should yield to avoid a crash, even if you are legally entitled to go.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Slightly to the right.,b:Sharply away from the curb.,c:Sharply toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb and let the vehicle roll back gently until the back of the front tire rests against the curb. This way, if the brakes fail, the curb will stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, how should you steer?
options: a:To keep the front wheels straight.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid.,c:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. As the vehicle starts to straighten out, be ready to steer smoothly as needed to keep control and avoid overcorrecting.

question: If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of your vehicle, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Flash your headlights and proceed.,b:Speed up to pass before they cross.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: When a pedestrian begins crossing in front of you, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Drivers are required to yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and should use extra caution, especially around children or anyone who may move unpredictably.

question: To pass a bicyclist safely, what should you do?
options: a:Drive into the bicycle lane until it is clear to pass.,b:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible when passing.,c:Honk to warn the bicyclist and then pass quickly.
note: To pass a bicyclist safely, slow down and give them as much space as possible, following your state’s minimum passing distance (often at least 3 feet, and more at higher speeds). Do not drive in the bicycle lane to pass, and avoid honking in a way that could startle the rider and cause a loss of control.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus on the opposite side of a divided highway with a median, must you stop?
options: a:False,b:True
note: On a divided highway with a physical median or barrier, you are generally not required to stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading on the opposite side. The median separates opposing traffic, so your lane is not considered to be passing the bus. Still, you should reduce speed and stay alert in case a child enters your side of the roadway.

question: If the driver ahead appears distracted (driving with one hand and talking), how should you react?
options: a:Match their behavior to keep pace.,b:Give that vehicle extra space.,c:Honk continuously until they pay attention.
note: If a driver ahead appears distracted, increase your following distance and give them extra space. Distracted drivers may brake suddenly, drift in their lane, or react slowly, so more space gives you time to respond safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On an interstate, when should you use the left lane?
options: a:To stop briefly,b:To overtake or pass another vehicle.,c:To prepare to exit.,d:To drive slower than the flow of traffic.
note: On multilane highways and interstates, the left lane is primarily for passing. Stay in the right lane for regular travel and move into the left lane only long enough to safely pass another vehicle, then return to the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What happens to fines for speeding in work zones?
options: a:Doubled.,b:Reduced.,c:Tripled.
note: In many states, fines for speeding and other moving violations are doubled in work zones when workers are present, and often in school zones during posted times. The higher fines are meant to protect vulnerable road workers and children.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, what is the correct action?
options: a:Make eye contact then proceed at normal speed.,b:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,c:Slow down and pass carefully in front of them.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway even if there is no marked crosswalk; stop and allow them to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and another vehicle arrive at a four-way stop at the same time and that vehicle is on your left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Whoever signals first has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. If the other vehicle is on your left, you are to that driver’s right, so you may proceed first after making sure the other driver is yielding.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey an instruction are called what?
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs tell you about laws and regulations you must obey, such as speed limits, stop signs, and yield signs. Ignoring these signs can result in traffic violations and penalties.

question: If your accelerator suddenly sticks while driving, you should:
options: a:Reach down to pull up the pedal.,b:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,c:Shift to park immediately.,d:Turn off the ignition while moving.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral, and apply steady pressure on the brakes. Steer to a safe place off the road and stop completely before turning off the engine. Do not reach down to pull the pedal or turn off the ignition while moving, as you can lose control.

question: By operating a motor vehicle in Nebraska, you have given implied consent to what?
options: a:Submit to a chemical test when requested by a law enforcement officer.,b:Refuse testing without consequence.,c:Choose which chemical test to take.
note: Under Nebraska’s implied consent law, by driving you agree to submit to chemical testing (such as breath, blood, or urine) when lawfully requested by an officer. Refusing a test can lead to license suspension and other penalties, even if you are not convicted of DUI.

question: What should you do when driving in foggy conditions?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of visibility.,b:Use your high beams to see farther ahead.,c:Turn on your low-beam headlights.
note: In fog, slow down and use low-beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in fog and can make it harder to see. Be prepared to reduce speed further or stop if visibility becomes very limited.

question: Under Nebraska law, children up to what age must be secured in a federally-approved child safety seat?
options: a:Four years old,b:Eight years old,c:Ten years old,d:Six years old
note: Nebraska law requires that children up to age six be secured in a federally‑approved child safety seat. Once a child is at least six, they may transition to a booster or seat belt as allowed by law, but younger children must always be in an appropriate child restraint system.

question: On a freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on a city street?
options: a:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.,b:In order to see potential hazards early.,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.
note: On a freeway, traffic moves faster and conditions can change quickly, so you need more time and space to react. Looking farther ahead lets you spot slowdowns, crashes, debris, and merging vehicles early so you can adjust speed or change lanes smoothly and safely.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street, what must you do?
options: a:Pull into the center lane and stop.,b:Slow down but stay in your lane and let it pass.,c:Drive faster to clear the road ahead.,d:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches from behind with lights and siren on, you must yield the right‑of‑way by moving as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop.

question: After a train has passed and you have stopped at the crossing, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Proceed immediately when you see the train pass.,b:Look for a second train.,c:Both look for a second train and wait for warning signals to stop flashing before proceeding.
note: After a train passes, another train may be coming on a different track, and warning devices may still be active. Always look carefully for a second train and wait until gates are fully raised and warning lights and bells have stopped before driving across the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As a green light turns yellow when you near an intersection, your best response is to:
options: a:Prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Apply the brakes sharply to stop immediately.,d:Turn right regardless of traffic
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should not speed up to beat the light. Instead, be prepared to stop if you can do so safely before the intersection; proceed only if you are too close to stop without hard braking or creating a hazard.

question: What can happen to bicyclists who do not obey traffic laws?
options: a:They are always given warnings instead of tickets.,b:They can be ticketed just like motor vehicle drivers.,c:They must ride on sidewalks only.,d:They are exempt from traffic laws.
note: Bicyclists are generally required to follow the same traffic laws as motor vehicle drivers, such as stopping at stop signs and obeying traffic signals. Because of this, they can be stopped and ticketed by law enforcement for violations, just like drivers of cars or trucks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, what must you ensure?
options: a:Be sure the passing lane is clear.,b:Pass only on the right.,c:Always watch for oncoming traffic.
note: On a multilane highway, you must be sure the lane you will use to pass is clear, signal, and change lanes only when it is safe. You normally pass on the left; passing on the right is allowed only in specific situations and when it can be done safely. Oncoming traffic is separated on a multilane divided highway, so your main concern is traffic in your lane and adjacent lanes.

question: Are children under age 18 allowed to ride in a vehicle's cargo area?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Nebraska law requires that children be properly restrained in a seat belt or appropriate child safety seat while the vehicle is moving. Riding in an unenclosed cargo area is unsafe and not permitted for passengers under 18 in normal travel, because they are not protected or properly restrained in a crash or sudden stop.

question: How should your following distance change when following a motorcycle?
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Keep it the same as any vehicle.,c:Ignore motorcycle behavior.,d:Increase your following distance compared to following other vehicles.
note: When following a motorcycle, you should increase your following distance compared with following other vehicles. Motorcycles can stop and swerve more quickly, and they are less visible. Extra space gives you more time to react if the rider brakes suddenly or needs to avoid a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a driver check blind spots when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Rely only on the left outside mirror.,b:Use only the rearview mirror.,c:Look over the left or right shoulder to view the blind spot.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot show, located just to the sides and slightly behind the vehicle. Before changing lanes, you must briefly turn your head and look over the appropriate shoulder to check these blind spots, in addition to using your mirrors and signal.

question: If someone is tailgating you and there is no right lane, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and ignore them.,b:Wait until the road ahead is clear and then slowly reduce speed to encourage them to pass.,c:Brake abruptly to warn them off.,d:Speed up to increase the gap from the tailgater.
note: If someone is following too closely and you cannot move to the right, keep a steady speed, increase your following distance ahead, and when the road ahead is clear, gradually slow down so the tailgater can pass safely. Never brake suddenly or speed up, as both can increase the risk of a collision.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign is used to:
options: a:Mark public recreation areas.,b:Indicate a stop requirement.,c:Provide mileage information.,d:Warn drivers of existing or possible hazards ahead.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert drivers to existing or possible hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or construction zones, so you can adjust speed and driving accordingly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Using a handheld device to read, type, or send written messages while driving in Nebraska is:
options: a:Completely legal if you are stopped at a red light.,b:A secondary offense with a fine of $200–$500.,c:A secondary offense with a $50–$100 fine.,d:A primary offense.
note: In Nebraska, using a handheld device to read, type, or send written messages while driving is a secondary offense, meaning you can be cited only if stopped for another violation. The fine for texting while driving is typically in the $50–$100 range for standard violations, not $200–$500. Regardless of the fine, you should never text while driving because it greatly increases crash risk.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,b:All of the above.,c:Tranquilizers
note: Many substances can impair driving, including prescription tranquilizers, illegal drugs, and common over-the-counter medicines such as cough syrups and cold tablets that contain codeine or antihistamines. These can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, and affect judgment. Always read medication labels and avoid driving if a drug may make you sleepy or less alert.

question: When approaching a blind pedestrian carrying a white cane or using a guide dog, a driver should:
options: a:Take the right-of-way.,b:Proceed normally.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog have the right-of-way. You must slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield so they can cross safely. Do not honk or rush them; wait until they are safely out of your path before proceeding.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You always have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing.,b:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.,c:You should put on cruise control near the crossing.
note: At railroad crossings, trains always have the right-of-way. You must stop when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or active warning devices such as flashing lights or gates. Never use cruise control near tracks; instead, slow down, look, and listen before crossing, and only proceed when you are sure it is safe and there is enough room to clear the tracks completely.

question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic as necessary. You do not have to stop unless needed for safety or to yield the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When backing up, how should you look?
options: a:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,b:Look directly through the rear window.,c:Press hard on the gas pedal and back quickly.
note: When backing up, turn your head and look directly through the rear window, checking over your shoulder for pedestrians, vehicles, and obstacles. Use your mirrors as helpers, not your only view, and back up slowly so you can stop quickly if something appears behind you.

question: What are truck “no zones”?
options: a:Zones where cars have plenty of following distance.,b:Areas several car lengths behind the truck.,c:Areas around large trucks where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close they limit the truck's ability to maneuver.,d:Designated safe zones for cars to pass trucks.
note: Truck no-zones are the large blind spots and close-in areas around big trucks where your car may not be visible to the truck driver or may be too close for the truck to stop or turn safely. Avoid lingering beside or directly behind trucks, and give them extra space for wide turns and longer stopping distances.

question: Double solid yellow center lines on a roadway indicate that passing is:
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Prohibited from either direction.,c:Allowed only if traffic is light.,d:Allowed only if you signal.
note: Double solid yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You must stay in your lane and may only cross these lines when making a permitted left turn into or out of a driveway or side road, if allowed by local law and when it is safe.

question: What minimum following distance should drivers maintain under normal conditions?
options: a:Five seconds.,b:Seven seconds.,c:Three seconds.
note: Allow at least three seconds of following distance under normal conditions and increase that distance when visibility or road conditions are poor.

question: What helps prevent drowsiness on long drives?
options: a:Slowing down and keeping a steady speed.,b:Drinking caffeinated beverages continuously.,c:Stopping regularly to rest and stretch.,d:Turning up the radio and keeping windows closed.
note: The safest way to prevent drowsiness on long trips is to stop regularly to rest, walk, and stretch. Short breaks help you stay alert and reduce fatigue. Caffeine, loud music, or opening and closing windows are not reliable ways to stay awake and can give a false sense of alertness.

question: True or False: It is illegal to drive at night using only your parking lights.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Driving at night with only your parking lights is illegal and unsafe. Parking lights are designed to make a parked vehicle visible, not to light up the road. When driving in the dark or when visibility is reduced, you must use your headlights so you can see the road and other drivers can see you.

question: A useful rule about passing is to:
options: a:Always try to reach the front of slow-moving traffic.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as necessary.,c:Pass anytime you are traveling faster than others.,d:Pass on the right whenever possible.
note: Safe drivers generally move with the flow of traffic within the speed limit and pass only when it is necessary and safe. Passing always carries extra risk because it places you in or near oncoming traffic, so you should avoid unnecessary passing and never pass on the right unless it is specifically allowed and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal turns steady yellow as you approach and you have not yet entered the intersection, you should:
options: a:Honk to warn cross traffic.,b:Proceed through at the same speed.,c:Come to a safe stop if you can do so.,d:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection and can stop safely, you must slow down and stop before the intersection. Only continue through if you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what does that signal signify?
options: a:Stop or slow down.,b:Turn right.,c:Turn left.
note: Hand and arm signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm straight out means a left turn. A left arm bent upward at the elbow means a right turn. A left arm extended downward with the palm to the rear means the driver is slowing or stopping.

question: When a law enforcement officer stops you for a traffic violation or equipment check, which document must you be able to produce?
options: a:Your driver license.,b:Proof of insurance.,c:Proof of registration.
note: Drivers are required to have and produce their operator's license when stopped; drivers are also responsible for providing proof of vehicle registration and insurance when requested.

question: What is the only thing that will reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time.,b:Coffee and rest.,c:Exercise at moderate intensity.
note: Only time lowers your BAC because your liver must metabolize the alcohol. Coffee, cold showers, food, or exercise might make you feel more awake, but they do not speed up how fast your body removes alcohol from your bloodstream.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view to the side is blocked at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed if you think it’s clear.,b:Stop and inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,c:Honk to warn approaching traffic.,d:Slow down and look both ways without stopping.
note: When buildings, parked cars, or other objects block your side view at an intersection, you must stop first. Then move forward slowly, inching out until you can clearly see cross traffic in both directions before you proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn across the median.,b:Proceed to the next exit.,c:Back up on the shoulder to reach the missed exit.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, stay calm and continue to the next exit. Never stop, back up on the shoulder, or make a U‑turn across the median; these maneuvers are extremely dangerous and illegal on freeways.

question: When should you slow down?
options: a:When the road is wet or slippery.,b:On narrow or winding roads.,c:At intersections or railroad crossings.,d:All of the above.
note: You should slow down in all of these situations: when the road is wet or slippery, on narrow or winding roads, and at intersections or railroad crossings. Reduced speed gives you more time to react and helps prevent skids or loss of control when traction or visibility is reduced.

question: A properly adjusted seat belt should fit how?
options: a:Is loose.,b:Is hidden beneath the seat.,c:Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
note: A lap belt should be snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen, not your stomach, so that in a crash the force is taken by the stronger pelvic bones. The shoulder belt should cross the middle of your chest and shoulder, away from your neck, and never be placed behind your back or under your arm.

question: What colors do warning signs (for upcoming hazards) use?
options: a:Black symbols or letters on a yellow background.,b:White symbols on a blue background.,c:Black symbols on a white background.,d:White letters on brown background.
note: Most general warning signs are yellow with black symbols or letters. These signs alert you to upcoming hazards such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings so you can slow down and be prepared. Work zone warning signs are similar but use an orange background with black symbols or letters.

question: What do broken white lines on the roadway indicate?
options: a:They indicate two-way traffic.,b:They separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:They mark a no passing zone.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross them when it is safe and legal to change lanes, but you should always check mirrors and blind spots and signal before moving.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow to a stop.,c:Keep driving normally until you find a service station.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, stay off the brakes, and gently ease your foot off the accelerator. Steer straight, let the vehicle slow down gradually, then carefully move to the side of the road and stop in a safe place. Slamming on the brakes can cause you to lose control, especially at higher speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, what should you do just before moving?
options: a:Check your side view mirror.,b:Check your rearview mirror.,c:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles.
note: Before changing lanes, first check your mirrors, then quickly turn your head to look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change. This head check lets you see into your blind spot, where another vehicle may be hidden from your mirrors.

question: If a child appears about to run into the street, what action should you take immediately?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn and be prepared to stop immediately.,b:Slowly inch forward to pass behind the child.,c:Turn on your parking lights and proceed cautiously.
note: If a child looks like they may run into the street, immediately cover the brake and be ready to stop while sounding a sharp blast of your horn to get their attention. Never try to inch past a child in the roadway; you must be prepared to stop completely to avoid a collision.

question: What color are warning signs that specifically alert drivers to pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds, schools, and school buses?
options: a:Yellow-green,b:Blue,c:Brown,d:Red
note: Fluorescent yellow‑green warning signs are used for pedestrian crossings, bicycle crossings, playground areas, and school and school‑bus related warnings because this color is highly visible and alerts drivers to areas where children and other vulnerable road users may be present.

question: What must you do when you approach a stopped school bus on your side of the road with red lights flashing?
options: a:Slow to 10 mph and proceed cautiously.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Change lanes and pass the bus carefully.
note: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Do not pass the bus, change lanes to go around it, or proceed at a reduced speed; children may be crossing the road in front of or behind the bus.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually which color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:White (many regulatory signs, such as speed limit and lane use signs),b:Green,c:Blue
note: Regulatory signs tell you about traffic laws and regulations that you must obey. Many regulatory signs, such as speed limit or lane use signs, are white with black or red symbols or lettering. However, some key regulatory signs use other colors, such as red octagonal STOP signs and red‑and‑white YIELD or DO NOT ENTER signs.

question: Double solid yellow lane markings indicate:
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:The lane to the right may pass.,c:Neither lane may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe and not prohibited by signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition is it legal to make a left turn at a red light after stopping?
options: a:When you are on a two-way street turning onto another two-way street.,b:When traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street (unless a sign prohibits it).,c:Whenever traffic is light and it seems safe.
note: In many U.S. jurisdictions, after stopping at a red light, you may turn left only when you are on a one‑way street turning onto another one‑way street, and only if there is no sign prohibiting the turn and the way is clear. You may not turn left on red from a two‑way street onto a two‑way street.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,b:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.,c:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop, or otherwise create a clear path, and remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by officials.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you slow down while exiting a highway?
options: a:On the main road just before the exit lane.,b:Once you have moved into the exit lane.,c:Once you see a toll booth up ahead.
note: Maintain highway speed until you are in the exit (deceleration) lane, then slow down to the posted advisory speed for the ramp. Braking on the main travel lanes before entering the exit lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: Accumulating 12 points against your license in two years will result in automatic revocation for how many months?
options: a:Three,b:Six,c:Nine
note: Accumulating 12 violation points in a two-year period leads to automatic revocation of an operator's license for six months.

question: You must yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian who is:
options: a:Only in a marked crosswalk.,b:Only if wearing reflective clothing.,c:Crossing any street in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.,d:Only if they are in an intersection.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks at intersections. An unmarked crosswalk exists at most intersections, even if there are no painted lines. For safety, you should be prepared to yield to any pedestrian crossing the street, especially where they have the legal right-of-way.

question: If a vehicle with high beams approaches you without dimming, where should you look?
options: a:Either side of the road equally.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Directly at the headlights to signal them.,d:At the center of the road.
note: When an oncoming vehicle does not dim its high beams, you should avoid looking directly into the bright lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This helps prevent temporary blindness from glare while still letting you track your lane position and stay safely on the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How many feet before your turn should you signal?
options: a:150 feet,b:100 feet,c:50 feet
note: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes to give other drivers time to react to your intentions.

question: Braking distance is affected by which factor?
options: a:The condition of your brakes and tires.,b:The condition of the pavement.,c:The speed your vehicle is traveling.,d:All of the above.
note: Braking distance is affected by several factors working together: your speed (higher speed greatly increases stopping distance), the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface (wet, icy, or gravel roads increase stopping distance). Because all of these matter, you must adjust your following distance and speed to match road and vehicle conditions.

question: Which statement about funeral procession escort vehicles is true?
options: a:They are not considered emergency vehicles.,b:They are emergency vehicles only when escorted by police.,c:They are classified as emergency vehicles.
note: Funeral escort vehicles may have special privileges under state law, but they are not generally classified as emergency vehicles like police, fire, or ambulances. However, when they display authorized lights or signals and are leading a funeral procession, you must still yield and avoid cutting through the procession, following any specific rules your state sets for funeral processions.

question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?
options: a:When following a small passenger vehicle.,b:When being tailgated by another driver.,c:When driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: You should increase your following distance whenever conditions increase your risk of a collision, such as when you are being tailgated. By opening up a larger gap in front of you, you give yourself more time to brake smoothly and reduce the chance that the tailgater will hit you if you must slow down or stop. Following distance is not increased just because the vehicle ahead is small; it is adjusted for risk factors like tailgaters, bad weather, poor visibility, or slippery roads.

question: To reduce glare from an oncoming vehicle's headlights, you should:
options: a:Flash your high beams at the oncoming driver.,b:Keep your eyes fixed on the centerline.,c:Glance briefly toward the right edge of the road and then refocus ahead.,d:Stare at the bright lights to adjust.
note: Avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights; glance toward the right side of the road briefly and then check ahead to maintain your lane position."

question: If another vehicle is in danger of hitting you, what is the best immediate action?
options: a:Wave your arms out the window.,b:Sound your horn to warn the other driver.,c:Turn off your headlights.
note: Use your horn to alert other drivers or pedestrians to imminent danger; it is an immediate and effective warning signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When arriving at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles to your right and left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your left.,b:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.,c:Yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. This rule helps decide who goes first when there are no signs or signals. If a vehicle is on your right, allow that driver to proceed first; if you are on someone else’s right, you have the right-of-way but should still proceed cautiously and be prepared to yield if another driver does not follow the rule.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent:
options: a:Is safe for drivers under 21.,b:Nearly doubles your chances of being involved in a fatal crash.,c:Has no effect on driving ability.,d:Is the legal limit for all drivers.
note: Even a low blood alcohol concentration, such as 0.02%, can affect driving by slowing reaction time and impairing judgment. Research shows that at about 0.02% BAC, the risk of being involved in a fatal crash is already significantly higher than at 0.00%. No amount of alcohol is considered completely safe for driving, and for drivers under 21, any measurable BAC can be illegal under zero-tolerance laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you required to signal every time you pull away from a curb?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You should always signal before pulling away from a curb so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know you are about to enter the traffic lane. Signaling gives others time to react and helps prevent collisions.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do with the ignition?
options: a:Set the parking brake.,b:Turn off the engine.,c:Turn off the engine, remove the key, and secure the vehicle from moving.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much more slowly than the flow of traffic, you will most likely:
options: a:Improve traffic flow.,b:Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,c:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can be dangerous because faster vehicles may need to brake or change lanes suddenly. If you must drive slower, stay in the right lane when possible and avoid unnecessarily blocking normal traffic flow, or you may be cited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:
options: a:The vehicle in front moves slightly right.,b:The oncoming lane line is broken.,c:The broken yellow line is next to your lane.,d:There is a no passing sign
note: On a two-way road with a broken yellow line next to your lane and a solid yellow line on the other side, you may pass when it is safe because passing is allowed from your side. Never cross double solid yellow lines to pass, and only pass when you have enough clear distance ahead.

question: When passing a recently parked vehicle on the roadside, you should:
options: a:Speed up to pass quickly.,b:Drive in the opposite lane to avoid it.,c:Slam on your brakes as you pass.,d:Assume the driver might open a door and use extra caution.
note: When passing a parked or recently parked vehicle, be prepared for someone to open a door or step out suddenly. Slow down if needed, leave extra space, and pass carefully to avoid a dooring or pedestrian collision.

question: Which action should you not omit when changing lanes?
options: a:Giving a turn signal.,b:Checking for other drivers who may also move into the same lane.,c:Driving faster than surrounding traffic.,d:Checking your side and rearview mirrors.
note: When changing lanes, you must always check your mirrors, check for other drivers who may also move into the same lane, and signal your intention. You should never drive faster than surrounding traffic just to make a lane change; instead, adjust your speed smoothly and safely while keeping with the general flow of traffic.

question: What message is shown on a red octagon-shaped sign?
options: a:One-way,b:Do not enter,c:Stop
note: An octagon-shaped red sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look to avoid glare?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road.,b:At the vehicle’s wheels.,c:Directly at the lights to signal them,d:Toward the right side of the road.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly into the lights. Instead, glance toward the right side of the road and use the edge line or lane markings as a guide. This reduces glare and helps you stay in your lane until the vehicle passes.

question: Are fines for speeding tripled in work and school zones?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Many states, including Nebraska, increase fines for speeding and other moving violations in work zones when workers are present and in designated school zones during restricted hours. These fines are commonly doubled, not tripled, to encourage drivers to slow down and protect workers and children.

question: If you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle while on a divided multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available.,b:Slow down,c:Stop immediately in your lane.,d:Speed up to avoid stopping in front of it.
note: On any road, including a divided multilane highway, you must yield the right-of-way to approaching emergency vehicles using lights and sirens. Safely slow down, move as far as practical to the right (or otherwise clear a path), and be prepared to stop until the emergency vehicle has passed. Never speed up or block its path.

question: A broken yellow centerline indicates what?
options: a:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line on your side is broken, you may cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if the lane is clear and it is safe and legal to do so. You must not pass if oncoming traffic is too close, visibility is poor, or signs prohibit passing.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Left,c:Right
note: On an uphill two-way road with no curb, turn your front wheels to the right, toward the edge of the road. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will roll off the pavement and the car will move away from traffic instead of into the roadway.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,b:Only when you are slowing down.,c:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
note: You should check your mirrors often so you always know what is happening behind and to the sides of your vehicle. Frequent mirror checks help you spot fast-approaching vehicles, lane changers, and emergency vehicles early so you can react safely.

question: Which statement about work zones is correct?
options: a:Work zones are indicated by blue signs.,b:You do not need to slow down in work zones if workers are not present.,c:Work zones may be stationary or moving and are marked with orange signs; drivers should slow down and be extra attentive.,d:Work zones are always stationary and marked with black and white signs.
note: Work zones are marked with orange signs and may be either stationary (like a fixed construction site) or moving (such as line-painting or mowing). Drivers must slow down, obey posted work-zone speed limits, and stay especially alert for workers, equipment, and sudden lane shifts.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicates what?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Traffic light ahead.,c:Do not pass.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you must not pass from your lane. It indicates that it is unsafe to move into the oncoming lane, often because of hills, curves, or limited visibility.

question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means you may:
options: a:Speed up to beat cross traffic.,b:Ignore pedestrians in the crosswalk.,c:Proceed through the intersection if it is safe and clear.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, but only if the intersection is clear and it is safe. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning right on a solid red light, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed because you have the right-of-way.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and turn only if not prohibited and safe.
note: Before turning right on a solid red light, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. After stopping, you must yield to pedestrians and all cross traffic, and only turn if there is no sign prohibiting a right turn on red and it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c:Traffic control devices.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see using your mirrors alone. To check these areas, you must quickly glance over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging to be sure no vehicle is hidden beside you.

question: Which action is unlawful regarding a stopped school bus displaying flashing red lights and its stop arm extended?
options: a:Passing within 100 feet of any intersection.,b:Passing within 100 feet of any railroad crossing.,c:Passing the bus.
note: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped. Passing the bus in this situation is unlawful because children may be crossing the road. Do not proceed until the bus moves again or the red lights and stop arm are turned off, except where specific state laws provide a divided-highway exception.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow, which lights are a good way to make your vehicle more visible?
options: a:Use only your instrument panel lights.,b:Use only your parking lights.,c:Turn on your low-beam headlights.
note: In conditions like dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, turning on your low-beam headlights makes your vehicle much easier for others to see. Parking lights or instrument panel lights alone do not provide enough visibility and often are not legal as a substitute for headlights in reduced-visibility conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from an alley or driveway across a sidewalk, what should drivers do?
options: a:Expect pedestrians to yield to your vehicle.,b:Proceed if no pedestrians are visible on the sidewalk.,c:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians.
note: When exiting an alley, driveway, or parking lot, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk area and look carefully for pedestrians. Pedestrians using the sidewalk have the right-of-way, and you must yield to them before continuing into the roadway.

question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve visibility without as much glare.

question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light indicates you may:
options: a:Not turn in that direction until the signal changes to green.,b:Turn after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:Turn after you come to a complete stop.,d:Turn if no other vehicles are present
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped; you may not turn in the direction of the arrow until it changes to green or a green arrow appears. Turning against a red arrow is prohibited unless specifically allowed by a sign in some jurisdictions.

question: It is important to frequently check the traffic behind you when you are:
options: a:Slowing down.,b:Driving down steep hills.,c:Changing lanes.,d:All of the above.
note: You should check traffic behind you regularly, not just when changing lanes. It is especially important to look in your mirrors when you plan to slow down, drive down steep hills, change lanes, back up, or stop suddenly. Knowing what is happening behind you helps you avoid being hit from the rear and lets you adjust your driving safely.

question: If you observe pedestrians in a crosswalk you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Continue; you have the right-of-way.,b:Wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing.,c:Pull to the right and go around them.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk and wait until the crosswalk is clear before proceeding.

question: True or False: When driving in fog you should use high beam headlights to see better.
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only on rural roads,d:Only if visibility is over 500 feet
note: High beams should not be used in fog because their light reflects off the water droplets and creates glare, making it harder to see. Use low-beam headlights or dedicated fog lights so the light stays lower on the road and improves your ability to see lane lines and other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving next to a single broken white line, you may:
options: a:Only cross during daylight,b:Only cross if you are in the left lane.,c:Cross the line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.,d:Not cross the line to pass.
note: A single broken (dashed) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

question: Vehicle stopping distances never depend on which factor?
options: a:Your own reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
note: Stopping distance is affected by your reaction time, your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, road surface, weather, and vehicle weight. The time of day by itself does not change how far your vehicle needs to stop; it is these physical and driver-related factors that matter.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow traffic light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you should be prepared to yield to pedestrians or other vehicles that may not be yielding correctly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a roadway with two or more lanes, how should you respond to a 'Merging traffic' sign?
options: a:Always remain at your present speed.,b:Speed up to avoid congesting traffic.,c:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes or adjusting speed when safe.
note: A 'Merging traffic' sign warns that vehicles will be entering your lane from an on-ramp or side road. You should help traffic flow smoothly by making room: if it is safe, change lanes away from the merge area or adjust your speed so merging drivers can enter without sudden braking or cutting in.

question: A good driver should monitor which areas around the vehicle?
options: a:Stare directly in front of their car.,b:Watch ahead, to the sides, and behind using mirrors.,c:Only focus on the middle of the road.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan in all directions: ahead, to both sides, and behind using mirrors. Focusing only straight ahead or only on the middle of the road can cause you to miss hazards like vehicles in adjacent lanes, pedestrians, or cyclists. Watching beside and around your vehicle helps you anticipate and react safely to changing traffic conditions.

question: True or False: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers and must obey traffic laws.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Bicyclists are considered vehicle operators and generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. They must obey traffic signals, signs, lane markings, and right‑of‑way rules. Motorists must treat bicycles as legitimate road users, giving them space and yielding when required, just as they would for other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn who must you yield the right-of-way to?
options: a:Pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Other drivers who are already in the intersection.,c:Oncoming traffic and any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, because they have the right‑of‑way unless they are stopped by a signal or sign. You must also yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection before you complete your turn. Do not start your left turn until it is safe and the way is clear of oncoming vehicles and crossing pedestrians.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:Yellow and white,c:White
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions, such as the center line on a two‑way road. White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction, such as lanes on a multi‑lane one‑way street or freeway. Knowing this color code helps you understand where passing is allowed and which direction traffic should be moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: Turning left on a red light is always prohibited.
options: a:True,b:False
note: In many states, you may turn left on a red light only from a one‑way street onto another one‑way street, after coming to a complete stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, and only if there is no sign prohibiting it. In all other situations, a left turn on red is not allowed, so you must wait for a green signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After you pass a vehicle on the left, you should not move back into the right lane until you can clearly see the front of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror and have enough space to return without cutting them off. This ensures you have fully cleared the other vehicle and reduces the risk of a collision if you need to slow down after returning to the lane.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:No passing is permitted from either lane.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane with the solid yellow line.,c:Traffic next to the broken line may pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.
note: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, the side with the broken line is allowed to pass when it is safe and clear, while the side with the solid line is not allowed to pass. This marking controls passing in each direction separately to reduce head‑on collision risk.

question: What happens to tires on a wet roadway as speed increases?
options: a:As you drive faster, your tires become less effective at clearing water.,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: As speed increases on a wet roadway, your tires have less time to squeeze water out from under the tread. This makes them less effective at gripping the road and increases the risk of hydroplaning, where the tires ride on top of the water and lose contact with the pavement.

question: When roads are snowy or icy, you should:
options: a:Drive as you would under normal conditions.,b:Use your cruise control.,c:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.
note: On snowy or icy roads, you should slow down and make all speed and steering changes gradually. Sudden braking, acceleration, or sharp steering can easily cause a skid because traction is greatly reduced on slick surfaces.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never take when changing lanes?
options: a:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,b:Move into another lane while inside an intersection.,c:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
note: You should not change lanes while you are driving through an intersection because traffic and signal changes make it more likely that another driver will not anticipate your movement. Instead, complete the intersection first, then change lanes when you are on the straightaway and can clearly see traffic around you. Always check mirrors and blind spots and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: What does a steady green light at an intersection allow you to do?
options: a:Must slow down and prepare to stop.,b:May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.,c:Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if it is safe and if there is no sign prohibiting the movement. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to oncoming traffic when turning left.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop.,b:Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.,c:Continue moving steadily and clear the intersection safely.
note: If the light turns yellow after you have entered the intersection, continue through and clear the intersection safely. Stopping suddenly in the intersection can cause rear‑end collisions and block cross traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate, what should you do after signaling?
options: a:Wait for the lane to clear before merging.,b:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed into the lane,c:Merge carefully into the gap.
note: When merging onto an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal, find a safe gap, and then merge smoothly. Do not assume other drivers will move over or slow down for you.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.,b:At all times.,c:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks and stop if needed to let them cross safely. Pedestrians do not need to signal or wave; the driver is responsible for watching for people in the crosswalk.

question: When parked facing uphill next to a curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.,b:Keep the front wheels straight ahead.,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb.,d:Turn your wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking facing uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: How must a driver handle pedestrians, even if they are not following the rules?
options: a:Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.,b:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of their vehicle.,c:Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.
note: Drivers must always do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting pedestrians, even when the pedestrian is crossing improperly. You should be prepared to slow, stop, or yield to prevent a collision, because a pedestrian is much more vulnerable than someone in a vehicle.

question: When is pavement especially slippery during rain?
options: a:Just after rain begins because oil and dirt mix with water.,b:After it has been raining for several hours.,c:Only when temperatures are below freezing.,d:When rain becomes a heavy downpour.
note: When rain first begins, water mixes with oil, grease, and dirt that have built up on the road surface, creating a very slick film. After it has rained for a while, much of this residue is washed away and traction usually improves, though you should still drive carefully in wet conditions.

question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a minimum BAC of:
options: a:0.02 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.08 percent.
note: In most U.S. states, including Nebraska, it is illegal for drivers 21 and older to operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher. You can still be impaired at lower levels, but 0.08% is the standard per se legal limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach the top of a hill, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up slightly.,b:Prepare to stop if necessary.,c:Maintain a steady speed.
note: As you approach the top of a hill, your view of oncoming traffic, stopped vehicles, or obstacles is limited. You should slow down, stay in your lane, and be prepared to stop if necessary because hazards may be hidden just beyond the crest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto a one-way street, you should start from which lane?
options: a:The lane closest to the left curb.,b:Any lane (as long as it is safe).,c:The lane in the center of the road.
note: When turning left from a one‑way street onto another one‑way street, you should start from the lane closest to the left curb. This keeps your path predictable and reduces conflicts with other traffic making different movements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter a freeway?
options: a:Drive slowly so you can check traffic thoroughly.,b:Signal and enter; freeway traffic must yield to you.,c:Signal and accelerate on the entrance ramp to match traffic speed, yielding to vehicles already on the freeway.
note: When entering a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to increase your speed to match the flow of traffic, signal, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Do not drive very slowly or expect freeway traffic to yield to you; you must merge only when it is safe.

question: What do broken yellow lines on the roadway indicate?
options: a:They separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate passing may be allowed.,b:They mark no-passing zones.,c:They separate lanes moving in the same direction.
note: Broken yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate that passing is allowed when it can be done safely and is not otherwise prohibited by signs or other markings.

question: Is it lawful to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other motor vehicle. You must not drive side‑by‑side with a motorcycle in the same lane because it reduces the motorcyclist’s space to maneuver and increases the risk of a collision.

question: When changing lanes, what should you do to check for vehicles in your blind spot?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely solely on the rearview mirror.,c:Rely only on the side mirror on the side you plan to move to.,d:Signal without checking.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This head check lets you see into your blind spot, where vehicles may be hidden from your mirrors.

question: Which of the following is not a safe interstate driving practice?
options: a:If you miss your exit, proceed to the next exit.,b:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,c:Change lanes without signaling.
note: On interstates, safe driving includes signaling before every lane change, keeping right if you are driving more slowly than other traffic, and continuing to the next exit if you miss yours. Changing lanes without signaling is unsafe and usually illegal.

question: To ensure your physical condition does not impair driving, you should:
options: a:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.,b:Drive within your physical limitations.,c:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.,d:All of the above.
note: All three actions are important for safe driving: staying physically fit and getting checkups, driving within your physical limits, and knowing how any medicine affects you. However, the key safety point most directly tied to immediate driving risk is understanding how medications (including prescriptions, over‑the‑counter drugs, and alcohol) affect your alertness, vision, and reaction time, and choosing not to drive if they impair you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a solid yellow centerline?
options: a:Only to make a left turn into a driveway, alley, or private road.,b:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.,c:At any time.
note: A solid yellow centerline means you must not cross it to pass other vehicles. You may cross a solid yellow line only to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, side road, or private road, or where signs or markings specifically allow it. Never use a solid yellow line side for passing.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are typically what color background?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:White.
note: Regulatory signs tell you about traffic laws and regulations, such as speed limits, lane use, turns, parking, and other requirements. These signs are typically white rectangles or squares with black or red lettering or symbols, making them easy to distinguish from warning (yellow) and guide (green) signs.

question: If an approaching train is close enough or fast enough to be a danger, you must do what?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Cross the tracks at your own risk.,c:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
note: If a train is close enough or moving fast enough to be a danger, you must stop and not cross the tracks. Wait until the train has completely passed and you can see that all tracks are clear in both directions before proceeding. Trains cannot stop quickly, and trying to beat a train is extremely dangerous and illegal.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the line dividing your lane from the one you want to enter is which type of line?
options: a:Solid yellow,b:Double solid yellow,c:Broken white
note: Broken white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a broken white line when it is safe to change lanes or pass. Solid or double solid yellow lines, by contrast, mark the center of two‑way roads and generally prohibit passing from the side with the solid line.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should drivers do?
options: a:Always stop,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: Pentagon-shaped school crossing signs warn that you are near a place where children may be crossing the road. You must slow down, watch carefully for children, and be ready to stop if they are in or near the crosswalk.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,b:Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop and may not be able to avoid a collision if you stop suddenly in front of them.,c:Large trucks and buses travel at a higher speeds than small vehicles.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than cars and need a longer distance to stop. If you brake suddenly in front of them, they may not be able to stop in time and could rear-end your vehicle. Always avoid cutting closely in front of large vehicles and making sudden stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:If you increase your speed before the turn.,b:Only if a sign explicitly permits the turn.,c:If the traffic on the street you are turning onto is moving to the left.
note: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street if traffic on the new street is moving to the left and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and make the turn from the left lane into the left lane of the new street.

question: If you are involved in a collision, what should you do first?
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:Call the police.,c:Help the injured.
note: If you are involved in a collision, you must stop immediately. Stopping is required by law and lets you check for injuries and damage. Once stopped, move to a safe place if possible, call emergency services, and give help to anyone who is injured without moving them unless there is immediate danger.

question: A steady green arrow displayed by a traffic signal means:
options: a:Traffic in the indicated lane must turn in the arrow's direction and has the right-of-way.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular green light and you may go straight or turn as you wish.,c:You may proceed in the arrow's direction only if a circular green light is also shown.,d:The arrow applies only on one-way streets.
note: A steady green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow. Traffic turning with the arrow has the right-of-way over oncoming traffic and pedestrians in conflict with that movement, but you must still proceed with caution and yield to anyone who is lawfully in the intersection.

question: When must you use your headlights?
options: a:Between sunset and sunrise and whenever visibility is reduced (such as in rain or fog).,b:Only after 8 p.m. and before 7 a.m.,c:Between 7 a.m. and 8 p.m.
note: Headlights must be used from sunset to sunrise and any time visibility is poor, such as in rain, fog, or snow, typically when you cannot see clearly about 500 feet ahead. Using headlights in low-visibility conditions helps other drivers see you and improves your own view of the road.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Loudly play the radio while driving so you won’t think about your argument.,b:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.,c:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.
note: Strong emotions like anger or stress can distract you, slow your reactions, and make you take risks you normally would not take. Before driving, take time to calm down so you can focus fully on the road and make safe decisions.

question: True or False: Drivers may park in handicap parking access aisles next to accessible stalls.
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only with a permit,d:Only if loading a passenger
note: Access aisles next to accessible parking spaces must always be kept clear. They provide extra room for wheelchair users and lifts to enter and exit vehicles safely, so parking or stopping there is not allowed, even with a permit or when loading a passenger.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals fail, how should you signal a turn?
options: a:Use your horn.,b:Use your headlights.,c:Use hand signals.,d:Flash your brake lights rapidly.
note: If your turn signals are not working, you must use standard hand and arm signals to show other drivers when you are turning or stopping. Clear hand signals help others anticipate your actions and reduce the risk of a collision.

question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A steady red arrow,b:A flashing yellow light,c:A green arrow pointing left,d:A solid green light
note: A steady green arrow for a left turn means you have a protected turn: oncoming traffic and pedestrians facing you are stopped by a red light, so you have the right-of-way to turn left, while still checking the intersection for any hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to which road users?
options: a:Traffic behind you only.,b:Only drivers signaling to exit the roundabout.,c:Vehicles already in the roundabout and any pedestrians or bicyclists in crosswalks.
note: You must yield to traffic already in the roundabout and also to pedestrians and bicyclists in crosswalks at the entrances and exits. Vehicles inside the circle have the right‑of‑way; entering traffic must wait for a safe gap and proceed only when it will not interfere with circulating vehicles or crossing pedestrians and cyclists.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down but do not stop.,b:Safely pull to the curb and stop to check if it is on your street.,c:Keep driving until you spot the vehicle.,d:Continue at the same speed and look in your mirrors
note: If you hear a siren and it sounds close but you cannot see the emergency vehicle, safely pull as far to the right as you can and stop. Stay stopped until you can tell where the vehicle is and whether it will be using your roadway. This helps keep the lane clear and prevents you from suddenly blocking the emergency vehicle’s path.

question: When an authorized emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights approaches, how should drivers respond?
options: a:Drivers should ignore the siren and continue driving.,b:Drivers must pull to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.
note: When an authorized emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and/or flashing lights, you must immediately yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe to reenter traffic, unless a police officer directs you otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.,b:Make room for the merging traffic,c:Always maintain your position.
note: When traffic is merging into your lane on a freeway, help keep traffic flowing smoothly and safely by making room when you can. Adjust your speed or change lanes if it is safe so the merging driver has a gap to enter. Do not speed up to block them or insist on your right‑of‑way; cooperation reduces sudden braking and collisions.

question: Why must drivers be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:Motorcycles are more likely to use their headlights only during the day.,b:Motorcycles always travel much slower than cars.,c:Motorcyclists rarely follow traffic laws.,d:Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see and may be hidden in blind spots.
note: Drivers must be especially alert for motorcycles because they are smaller and can be easily hidden by other vehicles, roadside objects, or in your blind spots. They can also appear farther away or slower than they really are, making their speed and distance harder to judge. Always check mirrors and blind spots carefully and allow extra following and passing space around motorcycles.

question: A driver license is considered:
options: a:A permanent entitlement,b:A guaranteed right.,c:An optional permit given to everyone.,d:A privilege that may be revoked for abuse.
note: Driving in the U.S. is legally treated as a privilege, not a guaranteed right. The state can suspend or revoke a driver license for violations such as DUI, excessive points, or failing to appear in court. Safe, lawful driving is required to keep this privilege.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane road, you cannot pass safely unless you:
options: a:Are able to clearly see the road ahead only.,b:Are in a hurry.,c:Can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic and can clearly see the road ahead.,d:Have a vehicle capable of high speed.
note: You may only pass on a two‑way, two‑lane road when you can clearly see enough clear road ahead and can complete the pass and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic. Never start a pass if you cannot safely move back into your lane in time, even if your vehicle is powerful.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Try to drive through the crossing quickly.,b:Maintain your speed and ignore warning signs.,c:Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop.
note: Approach railroad crossings cautiously: slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If warning lights are flashing, a train is visible, or gates are down or starting to lower, you must stop before the tracks—generally between 15 and 50 feet—and never drive around lowered gates.

question: What is a major cause of rear-end collisions in work zones?
options: a:Construction equipment obstructing drivers' views.,b:The lack of work zone barricades.,c:Driving at a different speed than surrounding traffic.
note: In work zones, many rear‑end crashes happen because drivers are going much faster or slower than the traffic around them, or they fail to adjust to sudden slowdowns. You should watch for signs, reduce speed in advance, and travel at a steady speed that matches the flow within the posted limits.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Apply the brakes hard and hold them down.,b:Turn on hazard lights and coast to a stop in the lane.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually before pulling off the road.,d:Pull over immediately without braking.
