note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly to keep the vehicle straight, ease off the accelerator, and let the car slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking; once you have control and your speed has dropped, carefully steer to the shoulder and stop in a safe place, then turn on your hazard lights.

question: Why must you use greater caution when driving at night?
options: a:Traffic volume is always higher at night.,b:Vehicles stop more quickly at night.,c:Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to see hazards, road markings, and pedestrians. Because you cannot see as far ahead, you should slow down, increase your following distance, and use your headlights properly from sunset to sunrise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Increase speed to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Stop before entering the intersection.,c:Slow down and proceed if the road looks clear.
note: A steady red traffic light means you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection, at the stop line, or before the crosswalk. You may only proceed when the light turns green and it is safe, or when a turn on red is specifically allowed and can be made safely after stopping.

question: Which lights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: In rain, fog, or snow, use low beam headlights. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help other drivers see you without excessive glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Using a handheld wireless device to read, type, or send written communication while driving is what type of offense?
options: a:Primary offense.,b:Not an offense.,c:Secondary offense.
note: In Nebraska, using a handheld wireless device to read, type, or send written messages while driving is a secondary offense. This means an officer must stop you for another violation first, but you can still be fined for the device use. Avoid any texting or reading messages while driving to keep your attention on the road.

question: You should allow extra following distance when you are:
options: a:When following a small passenger car.,b:When following a driver who cannot see directly behind their vehicle.,c:When following a station wagon.
note: You should leave extra following distance behind vehicles whose drivers cannot see directly behind them, such as large trucks, buses, and vehicles towing trailers. These vehicles have large blind spots and can block your view of the road ahead, so more space gives you extra time to react.

question: After overtaking another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:As soon as you signal.,b:After about three seconds.,c:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,d:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: After you pass another vehicle, you should not move back into the right lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This shows you have enough space ahead. Then check your mirrors and blind spot, signal, and return smoothly without cutting the other driver off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure for changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, and change lanes only when it is safe.,b:Signal and move lanes immediately without checking mirrors.,c:Check your mirrors but do not signal.
note: A safe lane change always follows the same sequence: first turn on your signal to show other drivers what you plan to do, then check your rearview and side mirrors, then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. If the lane is clear and it is safe, move smoothly into the new lane and turn off your signal.

question: When parking on any hill, what should you always do?
options: a:Turn your front wheels in the proper direction so the vehicle will roll into the curb or away from traffic if the brakes fail.,b:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park (or in gear for a manual).,c:Both a and b.
note: Whenever you park on a hill, you should always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in park (for an automatic) or in gear (for a manual). In addition, you must turn your front wheels in the correct direction so the car will roll into the curb or away from traffic if the brakes fail: turn wheels away from the curb when facing uphill with a curb, and toward the curb or road edge when facing downhill or when there is no curb.

question: When traveling through a construction zone, you should:
options: a:Slow down, obey all work-zone signs and flaggers, and avoid rubbernecking.,b:Stop to watch the workers if traffic is slow.,c:Decrease your following distance to clear the area quickly.
note: In construction zones, you must slow as needed, obey all posted work-zone speed limits and signs, and follow directions from flaggers. Maintain a safe following distance and stay alert for workers, equipment, and sudden stops. Avoid rubbernecking—do not slow down just to look at the work, because this increases the risk of crashes and traffic delays.

question: What does the term for the amount of alcohol in the blood refer to?
options: a:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).,b:Alcohol absorption index (AAI).,c:Implied consent (IC).,d:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is the measure of how much alcohol is in a person’s bloodstream, usually expressed as a percentage. As BAC increases, judgment, reaction time, and coordination become more impaired, and at or above the legal limit you can be arrested for driving under the influence.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on the interstate, slower-moving traffic should:
options: a:Drive with four-way flashers activated.,b:Stay in the left lane at all times.,c:Keep to the right.
note: On multi-lane highways and interstates, slower traffic should keep to the right so faster vehicles can safely pass on the left. This reduces lane changes and helps traffic flow smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action should you never take?
options: a:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Change lanes abruptly or without warning.,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: You should never change lanes abruptly or without warning. Safe lane changes require signaling, checking mirrors, and looking over your shoulder to check blind spots before moving into another lane.

question: Before returning to your lane after passing another vehicle, what should you confirm?
options: a:You have sounded your horn to signal your return.,b:You have flashed your lights to warn the other driver.,c:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space and do not cut off the other driver.

question: If drivers keep passing you on both sides while you're in the expressway center lane, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to match traffic.,b:Move into the lane to your right.,c:Move into the lane to your left.,d:Stay in the center lane.
note: If vehicles are passing you on both sides in the center lane, you are likely going slower than the flow of traffic. Move safely into the lane to your right so faster traffic can use the center and left lanes to pass.

question: Interstate driving requires which of the following?
options: a:Both of the above.,b:Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,c:Be constantly alert.
note: Interstate driving requires both the ability to safely handle higher speeds and the need to stay constantly alert. Traffic moves quickly and conditions can change fast, so you must be comfortable at freeway speeds and pay close attention at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in a business district?
options: a:30 miles per hour.,b:20 miles per hour.,c:25 miles per hour.
note: In most U.S. jurisdictions, including many state DMVs, the default speed limit in a business district is 25 mph unless signs say otherwise. Always follow the posted speed limit, but if no sign is present in a business area, you should generally assume 25 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The posted maximum speed limit should be driven under what conditions?
options: a:During the night.,b:Under ideal conditions.,c:During the day.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed for ideal conditions—good visibility, dry pavement, and light traffic. When conditions are poor, such as in rain, fog, heavy traffic, or at night, you must slow down to a speed that is safe for those conditions, even if it is below the posted limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum legal speed on Nebraska interstate highways under normal conditions?
options: a:50 mph.,b:60 mph.,c:40 mph.
note: On Nebraska interstate highways, a common posted minimum speed is 40 mph under normal conditions. You must not drive slower than the posted minimum unless weather, traffic, or road conditions make a lower speed necessary for safety.

question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:Because other drivers will pull in front of you to pass the large vehicle.,b:To get caught in the vehicle's slipstream and save fuel.,c:To see around the sides of the vehicle and have more time to react.
note: Large vehicles like trucks and buses block your view of the road ahead and need more distance to stop. By increasing your following distance, you can see farther around the vehicle, have more time to react to hazards, and maintain a safe stopping distance.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Find a safe place to stop and take a short nap.,b:Turn up the radio and open the windows.,c:Increase your speed to finish sooner.
note: Fatigue greatly reduces your reaction time and judgment. If you feel drowsy, the safe choice is to pull over at a safe location and rest or take a short nap. Tricks like turning up the radio or opening windows do not restore alertness and should not be relied on.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, who must you yield to?
options: a:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: When turning left, you must wait for oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and for pedestrians in or entering the crosswalk. Only turn when the way is clear and it is safe and legal according to any signals or signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: At a four-way stop, drivers must yield to motorists who arrived before them.
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: At a four‑way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrive. The first vehicle to stop has the right‑of‑way. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, how should you respond?
options: a:Maintain speed and steer aggressively to regain control.,b:Slam on the brakes immediately to stop as quickly as possible.,c:Steer straight and gradually slow by easing off the gas
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and slowly ease off the accelerator. Do not slam on the brakes. Once the vehicle is under control and slowing, move off the road to a safe place.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the normal speed limit in a residential district?
options: a:20 miles per hour.,b:30 miles per hour.,c:25 miles per hour.
note: In many U.S. states, the typical unposted speed limit in residential areas is 25 mph. Always follow the posted speed limit, as local laws may set a different speed for specific neighborhoods or streets.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Always come to a complete stop whether or not children are present.,b:Sound your horn to warn students.,c:Watch for children and be ready to stop.
note: A school crossing sign means you are near a place where children may be crossing the road. Slow down, watch carefully for children, and be ready to stop for pedestrians in the crosswalk or when directed by signs or crossing guards.

question: What can help you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Tailgate the vehicle in front of you to show displeasure.,b:Relax and focus on safe driving.,c:Drive faster to get past slow traffic.
note: Staying relaxed and focusing on safe driving helps you avoid aggressive behavior. Give yourself extra time, follow at a safe distance, obey speed limits, and don’t react emotionally to other drivers’ mistakes.

question: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving will:
options: a:Significantly increase your chances of being involved in a crash.,b:Not significantly increase your chances of being involved in a crash.
note: Talking or texting on a phone while driving takes your eyes, hands, and mind away from driving. This distraction greatly increases your risk of a crash, so you should avoid using a phone while driving whenever possible.

question: All children under age 18 in Nebraska are required to:
options: a:Ride in the front seat only.,b:Wear only lap belts,c:Always sit in the back seat.,d:Be secured in a safety belt or child safety seat.
note: Nebraska law requires that everyone under 18 be properly secured in a safety belt or an appropriate child safety seat. Proper restraints greatly reduce the risk of injury in a crash.

question: If you approach a flashing red traffic light, what is required?
options: a:May not proceed until it changes to green.,b:Treat the intersection as if it were controlled by a stop sign.,c:You are traveling in the wrong direction.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop at the proper place, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: Your speed does not affect the distance your vehicle travels after you apply the brakes.
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only at night,d:Only at high speeds
note: Your speed has a major effect on stopping distance. The faster you go, the longer it takes to stop after you hit the brakes, because your vehicle has more momentum and needs more distance to slow down safely.

question: When parking next to a curb, when should you signal?
options: a:When pulling next to,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb.
note: You should always signal both when pulling toward a curb and when leaving it. Signaling lets other drivers and cyclists know you are changing position in the roadway so they can adjust safely.

question: If you experience a sudden tire blowout, what is the recommended braking technique?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Use the brakes lightly.,c:Apply the brakes firmly.
note: In a sudden tire blowout, grip the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and ease off the accelerator. Once the vehicle is under control and slowing, use the brakes lightly to continue slowing and move off the roadway. Hard or abrupt braking can cause loss of control, especially with a blown tire.

question: If you must slow down on a slippery road, the first action to take is to:
options: a:Shift into neutral.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and immediately.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,d:Apply the parking brake.
note: On a slippery road, the safest first step is to take your foot off the gas pedal. This lets the vehicle slow gradually without upsetting traction. If you need to slow more, brake gently and steadily to avoid skidding.

question: If poor weather sharply reduces visibility, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: When visibility is sharply reduced by weather, slow down and increase your following distance. The extra space gives you more time to see hazards and stop safely if traffic ahead slows or stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When another vehicle is passing your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Pull as far to the right as possible without leaving the pavement.,b:Stay in your lane and reduce your speed.,c:Stay in your lane and maintain your speed unless there is an emergency.
note: When another vehicle is passing you, stay in your lane and maintain a steady speed so the other driver can judge the pass safely. Do not speed up. Only slow or move right further if needed to avoid a collision or if the lane is too narrow.

question: May you drive around lowered crossing gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When the lights have stopped flashing.,b:When the train has passed.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates. Stay stopped until the lights stop flashing, the train has passed, and the gates are fully raised and the roadway is clearly safe before proceeding.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips along the roadway?
options: a:To test a vehicle’s shock absorbers.,b:To slow traffic with a rough surface.,c:To alert inattentive drivers by vibration and sound that they have left the travel lane or are approaching a hazard.,d:To inform drivers of tire pressure problems.
note: Rumble strips are grooved or raised patterns on the road that create noise and vibration when you drive over them. They are designed to alert drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard such as a stop sign, toll plaza, or work zone.

question: Is it safe to use cruise control while driving on snowy or icy roads if you reduce speed?
options: a:True,b:False
note: On snowy, icy, or otherwise slippery roads, you should not use cruise control. You need full control over your speed so you can quickly reduce throttle and adjust to changing traction; cruise control can keep applying power when the wheels start to slip, making a skid or loss of control more likely.

question: Which of the following is a safe technique for driving through a curve?
options: a:Maintain the same speed throughout the curve.,b:Speed up as you enter the curve to maintain momentum.,c:Slow down as you enter the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.
note: For safe cornering, slow down before you enter the curve, then gently accelerate as you come out of it. Entering too fast or speeding up into the curve can cause you to lose traction and drift out of your lane, especially on wet or uneven pavement.

question: When lanes are separated by double solid yellow lines, what is allowed?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the left.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the right.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean you may not cross them to pass from either direction. They separate traffic moving in opposite directions where visibility or conditions make passing unsafe. You must stay in your lane unless making a permitted turn across the lines where allowed by local law.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best action?
options: a:Get out of the car and walk for help.,b:Stay in your car and wait for help.,c:Walk into the road to attract drivers' attention.
note: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, you should stay with your vehicle. The car provides shelter, is easier for rescuers to see than a person on foot, and offers some protection from cold and wind. Run the engine only periodically for heat, keep the exhaust pipe clear of snow to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning, and wait for help.

question: Children up to what age are prohibited from riding in cargo areas of vehicles?
options: a:12 years old.,b:18 years old.,c:10 years old.
note: In Nebraska, children under 18 are generally prohibited from riding in the cargo area of a vehicle because it is extremely unsafe and offers no proper restraint or protection in a crash. All children must be properly restrained in an appropriate seat or safety belt while the vehicle is moving.

question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is correct?
options: a:Opening a window and turning on the radio will reliably keep them alert.,b:Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly they may appear intoxicated.,c:Drinking strong coffee will immediately restore full driving ability.
note: Drowsy drivers can be as dangerous as drunk drivers. Fatigue slows reaction time, reduces awareness, and can cause drivers to drift out of their lane or even fall asleep, making their driving appear similar to someone who is intoxicated. Tricks like opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking coffee do not reliably make a drowsy driver safe; the only real solution is rest.

question: In Nebraska, the BAC limit for drivers under age 21 is:
options: a:0.1 percent.,b:0.02 percent.,c:0.08 percent.
note: Nebraska has a zero-tolerance law for drivers under 21. A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02% or higher is considered a violation for underage drivers. Because any amount of alcohol can impair judgment and reaction time, young drivers must not drive after drinking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: Drivers may pass on a two-lane roadway marked with a single solid yellow line on their side of the centerline.
options: a:True,b:Only during daylight,c:Only with turn signals,d:False
note: On a two-lane road, a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you may not pass. The solid line indicates that sight distance or other conditions make passing unsafe. Passing is only allowed from the side that has a broken yellow line, and only when it can be done safely.

question: If you begin to feel drowsy while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Take some caffeine pills.,b:Take a break.,c:Try to fight it.
note: If you start to feel drowsy while driving, the safest choice is to stop driving and take a real break. Pull over at the first safe place, rest, switch drivers if possible, or take a short nap. Caffeine or trying to fight sleep are not reliable and can lead to falling asleep at the wheel.

question: True or False: A motorist making a left turn must yield to a bicyclist entering the intersection from the opposite direction.
options: a:True,b:False
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, including bicyclists approaching from the opposite direction. Treat bicycles like any other vehicle in this situation: wait until the bicyclist has cleared the intersection and it is clearly safe before completing your turn.

question: True or False: Motorists are not required to yield to pedestrians who cross against the traffic signal.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Even if a pedestrian is crossing against the signal or outside a crosswalk, drivers must still do everything they reasonably can to avoid hitting them. Pedestrians may be violating the law, but motorists have a continuing duty to use due care and yield or stop when necessary to prevent a collision.

question: What does a steady red arrow indicate to drivers?
options: a:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction without stopping.,b:Drivers cannot proceed in the direction indicated by the arrow.,c:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after stopping.
note: A steady red arrow means you may not go in the direction the arrow points. You must stop and remain stopped for that movement until the signal changes. Only when the arrow turns green (or a permitted turn is otherwise indicated by your state’s rules) may you proceed in that direction.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A rectangular red sign.,b:A circular green sign.,c:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,d:A reflective orange triangular emblem
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle with a red border, mounted on the rear of vehicles that usually travel 25 mph or less, such as farm equipment. When you see this emblem, be prepared to slow down and pass only when it is safe and legal.

question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:
options: a:Maintain normal speed.,b:Yield only to pedestrians.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Come to a complete stop every time.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with extra caution. You do not have to stop unless another sign, signal, or traffic condition requires it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, what should a driver do?
options: a:Always come to a full stop regardless of other traffic.,b:Maintain speed and proceed unless another vehicle honks.,c:Yield to traffic already in the intersection and to traffic approaching from the right; be prepared to stop to avoid a crash.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), you must slow down, be ready to stop, and yield to traffic already in the intersection and to vehicles approaching from your right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent conflicts when no control devices are present.

question: How should drivers respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop, then proceed.,c:Increase speed to clear the area quickly.,d:Treat it the same as a red light.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns of a hazard or a need for extra caution. You should slow down, look carefully for other traffic, pedestrians, or obstacles, and proceed only when it is safe. A complete stop is not required unless other conditions demand it.

question: Is it lawful to operate a motor vehicle with a television screen visible to the driver?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Nebraska law prohibits operating a motor vehicle when the vehicle is equipped with a television or video screen visible to the driver.

question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Go through as soon as the train passes.,b:Wait to proceed until you have a clear view of all tracks.,c:Stop on the first railroad track and watch for another train.
note: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, you must not proceed as soon as the first train passes. Wait until you can clearly see down all tracks in both directions and are sure no other trains are approaching before crossing.

question: By law, how much lateral space must motorists leave when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Two feet,b:One foot,c:Three feet,d:No set distance
note: When passing a bicyclist, you must leave at least three feet of space between your vehicle and the bicycle. This buffer helps protect the rider from wind blast, driver error, or sudden swerves and should be maintained until you are safely past.

question: When driving at night, what should you do to drive more safely?
options: a:Always use high beams regardless of other vehicles.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Look directly into oncoming headlights.,d:Follow the taillights of the car ahead closely.
note: At night your visibility is reduced, so you need more time and space to react. Increasing your following distance gives you a larger safety cushion. Use low beams around other traffic, high beams only when appropriate, and avoid looking directly into oncoming headlights.

question: Construction zone signs typically have what shape and colors?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange background and black symbols.,b:Square with white and red coloring.,c:Round with black and yellow coloring.,d:Pentagonal with yellow-green background
note: Temporary construction and work zone signs are usually orange with black symbols or lettering. They are most often diamond-shaped, but may also be rectangular, and warn you of road work, lane shifts, workers, or equipment ahead.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Be ready to use your horn.,b:Drive more slowly than usual.,c:Allow a larger following distance than you would for a car.
note: Motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly than larger vehicles and offer less protection to their riders. Leave at least a three- to four-second following distance so you have enough time to react if the motorcycle slows or swerves suddenly.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, which response is safest?
options: a:Get out of their way.,b:Challenge them.,c:Speed up.
note: If you encounter an aggressive driver, do not engage with them. The safest response is to stay calm, move out of their way, and let them pass. Avoid eye contact, gestures, or racing, and if you feel threatened, contact law enforcement when it is safe to do so.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, what is important to remember?
options: a:Trucks require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.,b:Trucks require a smaller turning radius than cars.,c:Trucks always travel slower than passenger cars.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need more distance to come to a complete stop and extra room to turn. When driving near trucks, avoid cutting in front of them, don’t follow too closely, and give them plenty of space for braking and turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a roundabout, you should:
options: a:Enter the circle without yielding,b:Yield to traffic already within the roundabout.,c:Increase your speed.
note: At a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to traffic already in the circle. Vehicles inside the roundabout have the right-of-way, and you enter only when there is a safe gap. Traffic in U.S. roundabouts moves counterclockwise, so vehicles will be coming from your left.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When stopped at a red light that displays a green arrow, you may proceed in the arrow's direction if:
options: a:You are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.,b:You first come to a complete stop.,c:You wait until the light changes.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow if you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear. You do not have to wait for the circular light to turn green, but you must still yield to any pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, what is the general rule for who goes first?
options: a:The driver who arrives first proceeds first.,b:Drivers may insist on the right-of-way even if unsafe.,c:Drivers should always yield to vehicles on the left.
note: At a four-way stop, the vehicle that arrives first goes first after stopping. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Even when you have the right-of-way, you should proceed only when it is clearly safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On the interstate, vehicles are entering from an entrance ramp on your right. What should you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane and maintain a safe, steady speed; change lanes or adjust speed only if it is safe to help them merge.,b:Immediately merge left whenever you see vehicles on an entrance ramp.,c:Increase your speed sharply to prevent merging vehicles from entering.
note: On interstates, drivers entering from an on‑ramp must yield to traffic already on the highway. You should maintain a steady speed and lane position unless it is safe and easy to move left to create space. If you can safely change lanes or slightly adjust your speed to help them merge smoothly, that is courteous, but your primary duty is to stay predictable and avoid sudden lane changes or speed changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: It is legal to exceed the posted speed limit when passing another vehicle.
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must obey the posted speed limit at all times, even when passing another vehicle. Passing is not a valid reason to exceed the speed limit; going faster than the posted limit is illegal and can greatly increase crash risk.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use which lights?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or sleet, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can create glare, making it harder for you to see and for others to see you. Parking lights alone are not sufficient for visibility or safety.

question: True or False: You may never drive through, around, or under a railroad gate or barrier.
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must never drive through, around, or under lowered railroad gates or barriers. Trains cannot stop quickly, and going around the gate is both illegal and extremely dangerous. Always wait until the gates are fully raised and warning signals have stopped before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, which driver has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.,b:One driver should continue driving without stopping.,c:The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop, the driver who arrives first has the right-of-way after coming to a complete stop. If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first. When in doubt, communicate with eye contact and proceed cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic but your light is green, you should:
options: a:Follow the vehicle ahead into the intersection.,b:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,c:Turn left to find another route immediately.,d:Stop in the intersection and wait
note: Even with a green light, you must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it. If traffic ahead is stopped and would trap you in the intersection, wait behind the stop line until there is enough space to move all the way through without blocking cross traffic.

question: What is the only effective way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink black coffee to sober up quickly.,b:Take a brisk walk to burn off alcohol.,c:Allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol.
note: Only time decreases BAC; stimulants or activities cannot remove alcohol from your bloodstream or sober you up.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what are you allowed to do?
options: a:You must stay within your lane.,b:You may change lanes only from the left lane.,c:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes going the same direction; you may cross them to change lanes or pass when it is safe.

question: Which of the following is a dangerous habit when driving through work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle.,b:Both of the above.,c:Failing to watch for workers and moving equipment.
note: In work zones you must avoid any behavior that increases risk, including following too closely and not watching for workers or equipment. Both tailgating and inattention can quickly lead to rear‑end crashes or hitting workers in the lane, so you must slow down, increase following distance, and stay alert.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light with a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow’s direction?
options: a:You wait until the light changes.,b:You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.,c:You first come to a complete stop.
note: A green arrow indicates you may proceed in that direction from the appropriate lane when the way is clear; yield to any pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop before entering the intersection.,b:Yield just to the traffic on the right.,c:Yield the right-of-way to traffic in the roadway you are entering.
note: A yield sign requires you to slow down and yield to traffic and pedestrians in the roadway you are entering; stop only if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited in which locations?
options: a:On hills and curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.,b:Only on hills.,c:Only in school zones.,d:Only at night
note: Passing is illegal and unsafe where you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic or where conflicts are likely, such as on hills and curves with limited visibility, at intersections, and at railroad crossings. These areas have higher crash risk because other vehicles, trains, or crossing traffic may appear suddenly.

question: When parking facing uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,b:Leave the front wheels straight.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking facing uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will gently roll into the curb and stop the car from moving into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Slow down dramatically and drift into the lane.,b:Only glance at the inside rearview mirror.,c:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, signal, and then move only when the lane is clear. This sequence helps you see vehicles that may not appear in your mirrors and prevents cutting off other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Excessive speed most often leads to what?
options: a:Increases your ability to react to a hazard.,b:Often leads to high-risk decision-making.,c:Does not increase the chance of a crash.
note: Excessive speed reduces the time you have to see hazards and react, increases stopping distance, and makes crashes more severe. Drivers going too fast are more likely to make risky choices, such as late lane changes or hard braking, which raises crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A speed limit denotes what?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel under dangerous conditions.,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel under ideal conditions.,c:The suggested speed to travel under ideal conditions.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speed allowed under ideal conditions. You must slow down below the limit when conditions are poor, such as in rain, fog, heavy traffic, or road work, to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your vehicle end up?
options: a:In the left lane of the one-way street.,b:In the right lane of the one-way street.,c:In the center of the street.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the leftmost lane of that one-way street, closest to the lane you came from.

question: An orange and red triangular sign mounted on the back of a vehicle means what?
options: a:Shoulder work ahead.,b:Slow-moving vehicle.,c:The vehicle has the right-of-way.
note: An orange and red reflective triangle on the back of a vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle emblem. It warns that the vehicle usually travels 25 mph or less, such as farm machinery or road maintenance equipment, so you should slow down and pass only when it is safe and legal.

question: When approaching snow removal equipment on the roadway, what should you do regarding following distance?
options: a:Follow closely to pass quickly.,b:Maintain at least 100 feet of following distance.,c:Drive alongside the equipment until it turns off the roadway.
note: You should stay well back from snowplows and other snow removal equipment. Keeping at least about 100 feet of following distance helps you avoid blowing snow, flying debris, and sudden stops, and gives you more time to react if the equipment changes speed or direction.

question: What should you do with your speed when making a turn?
options: a:Keep your speed exactly the same.,b:Reduce your speed to a controllable level.,c:Brake hard during the turn.,d:Increase your speed to maintain momentum.
note: Before entering a turn, slow to a speed that lets you stay in your lane and maintain full control of the vehicle. Do most of your braking before the turn, then steer smoothly through it. Entering a turn too fast or braking hard while turning can cause skids or loss of control.

question: Nebraska law requires reporting a crash within how many days if there is injury, death, or apparent damages exceeding a dollar amount?
options: a:Five days / $250,b:10 days / $1,000,c:15 days / $750
note: Nebraska requires that a crash be reported to the Department of Roads within 10 days if anyone is injured or killed, or if it appears that there is more than $1,000 in total property damage. Reporting ensures that serious crashes are documented and that insurance and legal responsibilities can be handled properly.

question: Barricades, vertical panels, drums, and cones are commonly used to guide drivers through work zones. True or false?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Work zones commonly use barricades, vertical panels, drums, and cones to channel and guide traffic safely around construction or maintenance areas. Drivers must slow down, follow the devices and signs, and proceed with extra caution to protect workers and other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roundabout, when should you go?
options: a:Immediately,b:After coming to a complete stop regardless of traffic.,c:Only when there is an adequate gap in circulating traffic.
note: At a roundabout, you must slow down, yield to traffic already circulating, and enter only when there is a safe gap. You do not stop if traffic is clear, and you never force your way in; wait until you can merge smoothly without causing other drivers to brake hard.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Activate your four-way flashers.,b:Increase your speed so as not to impede traffic.,c:Stay alert
note: In work zones, stay alert for workers, equipment, lane shifts, and sudden stops. Reduce speed as posted, increase following distance, obey flaggers and signs, and be prepared to stop unexpectedly. Avoid distractions so you can react quickly to changing conditions.

question: What are the penalties for failing to secure child passengers properly?
options: a:No penalty for first offense,b:Two points plus court costs.,c:Two points assessed against the driver.,d:A fine and one point assessed against the driver.
note: States generally impose a fine and may assess license points when a driver fails to properly secure a child in an approved restraint. The key safety rule is always to use the correct child seat or booster for the child’s age, weight, and height, and to install it according to manufacturer and state requirements. Specific fine amounts and point values vary by state law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the correct lane, what should you do?
options: a:Turn from your current lane after signaling.,b:Go to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.
note: You must never make sudden, last‑minute turns or cut across lanes to avoid missing a turn. If you are not in the correct lane when you reach an intersection, continue straight, then go to the next intersection and make your turn from the proper lane when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is not working and no officer is present, how should you treat the intersection?
options: a:Treat the intersection as an all-way stop.,b:Allow traffic on major streets to proceed without stopping.,c:Treat the intersection as if it is controlled by yield signs.
note: When a traffic signal is completely dark and no officer is directing traffic, you must treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop in all directions, then proceed in turn when it is safe, yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians who arrived first or are already in the intersection.

question: What may occur if alcohol is taken together with another drug?
options: a:Both effects will always be reduced.,b:Both will cancel out and produce no effect.,c:The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be increased.
note: Alcohol taken with many other drugs can greatly increase the effects of both substances. This can slow your reaction time, reduce coordination, and impair judgment far more than either alcohol or the drug alone, making driving extremely dangerous.

question: Which of these is a place you should never park?
options: a:In a designated handicap space when you have a permit.,b:On a hill with a curb and set parking brake.,c:In front of a public or private driveway.
note: You must never park in front of a public or private driveway because it blocks access for vehicles entering or leaving. Parking is allowed in a marked accessible (handicap) space only if you have a valid permit and follow posted rules, and parking on a hill is allowed when you park legally and secure the vehicle properly.

question: Blue-colored traffic signs provide information about:
options: a:Construction and maintenance zones.,b:Motorist services such as rest areas,c:Mileage distances to cities only.,d:Regulatory requirements.
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals, helping drivers find essential services along the road.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:The same as daytime driving.,b:Legal only on major roads.,c:More dangerous because visibility is reduced and more impaired or tired drivers may be on the road.,d:Less dangerous due to lighter traffic.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because you cannot see as far or as clearly, making it harder to spot hazards in time. Glare from headlights can further reduce visibility, and there is a higher chance of encountering tired or impaired drivers after dark.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Drivers of small vehicles cannot see trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,b:Large trucks and buses usually travel faster than passenger cars.,c:Large trucks and buses have air brakes and cannot stop as quickly as smaller vehicles.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than passenger cars and use air brake systems that take slightly longer to activate. Because of their size and weight, they need a much longer distance to stop. If you stop suddenly in front of them, they may not be able to stop in time to avoid a rear-end collision.

question: What must you do when a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone?
options: a:Ignore the flagger and follow the surrounding traffic.,b:Follow the flagger's directions.,c:Assume the flagger is not authorized to direct traffic.
note: Flaggers are authorized to control traffic in work zones. Their directions have the same legal force as traffic signals or signs. You must follow their hand signals or signs to protect road workers and other drivers and to keep traffic moving safely through the construction area.

question: When vehicles are merging from on-ramps to your right on an interstate, the best action to avoid conflict is to:
options: a:Move to the right lane and slow significantly.,b:Maintain your current speed and lane.,c:Brake sharply to let them in.,d:Change lanes to the left when traffic allows.
note: If safe, move out of the right-hand lane to allow merging traffic from on-ramps to enter the freeway smoothly.

question: If you pass a stopped emergency or road assistance vehicle using flashing lights, what must you do if possible?
options: a:Move into a lane at least one travel lane away from the stopped vehicle, if possible.,b:Stop.,c:Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle.
note: When practical and legal, move at least one lane over away from stopped emergency or maintenance vehicles using flashing lights; otherwise slow down and pass with care.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no lights or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Cross immediately and quickly.,b:Always stop before crossing.,c:Prepare to yield to any approaching train and ensure there is room to clear the tracks.
note: At a railroad crossing without lights or gates, you are not required to stop every time, but you must approach with caution. Slow down, look and listen for trains in both directions, be prepared to yield, and never start across unless you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to completely clear the tracks on the other side.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what does that signal mean?
options: a:Turn left.,b:Come to a stop.,c:Turn right.
note: Hand and arm signals are used when turn signals cannot be seen or are not working. A left arm straight out means a left turn. A left arm bent upward at the elbow means a right turn. A left arm bent downward at the elbow means slowing or stopping. If you see a driver’s left arm and hand extended upward, you should expect that vehicle to turn right.

question: What color are temporary signs used in construction and maintenance work areas?
options: a:Red.,b:Yellow.,c:Orange.
note: Work zone and temporary construction signs are orange with black symbols or lettering. This bright color warns drivers of changing road conditions, lane shifts, workers on or near the roadway, and other construction-related hazards. When you see orange signs, slow down, stay alert, and be prepared for sudden stops or changes in traffic patterns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, yield the right-of-way to a driver who:
options: a:Arrived before you,b:Is across from you,c:Is on your left,d:Is turning left
note: At a four-way stop, each driver must stop and then proceed in the order of arrival. You must yield to any vehicle that stopped before you. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right. When facing each other, and arriving at the same time, a driver turning left yields to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Passing in any marked no-passing zone or within the prohibited distances of crossings and intersections.,b:Passing more than one vehicle at a time.,c:Passing on multilane highways.,d:Passing only during daylight
note: Passing is illegal in marked no-passing zones and within certain distances of intersections, railroad crossings, bridges, and hills where visibility is limited. These restrictions exist because oncoming traffic may not be visible or there may not be enough space to pass safely. Only pass where it is legal, where you have a clear view ahead, and where you can complete the maneuver without exceeding the speed limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You approach an intersection showing a steady yellow light and have not entered the intersection. What should you do?
options: a:Proceed through at the same speed.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Make a sudden lane change.,d:Prepare to stop safely and do so if possible.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you should slow down and stop if you can do so safely before the stop line or crosswalk. You should not speed up to “beat” the red light, because the light may change while you are in the intersection and increase the risk of a crash.

question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving:
options: a:Does not affect driving ability.,b:Is a distracting activity that can take your hands or attention off the wheel.,c:Is only prohibited for new drivers,d:Is recommended to stay alert.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction because it takes at least one hand off the wheel and your eyes and attention away from the road. Any activity that diverts your focus, even briefly, increases your risk of a crash.

question: When riding in a vehicle, which is the correct requirement for small children?
options: a:They should be secured in an appropriate child safety seat.,b:They are safe standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,c:They may be safely held by a strong adult.
note: Small children must be secured in a properly installed, federally approved child safety seat that is appropriate for their size and age. Holding a child or letting them stand is extremely dangerous because, in a crash, no adult can safely restrain a child against the forces involved.

question: What do flashing arrow panels in work zones typically indicate?
options: a:They are only used on interstate highways.,b:They guide drivers into certain lanes and indicate that part of the roadway is closed.,c:They direct drivers to stop immediately on the shoulder.
note: Flashing arrow panels in work zones are used to warn that a lane is closed ahead and to guide drivers into the correct open lane. They help you merge safely and avoid driving into closed or hazardous areas in the work zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you always use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when other vehicles are nearby.,b:When changing lanes.,c:Never in parking lots.
note: You must always use your turn signal when changing lanes so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know your intentions. Signaling early and consistently helps prevent collisions by giving others time to react to your movement.

question: When making an emergency roadside stop, what should you do before exiting the vehicle?
options: a:Leave the vehicle running and exit immediately.,b:Shift to park and set the parking brake.,c:Flash your headlights to warn other drivers.
note: Before exiting your vehicle during an emergency roadside stop, you should pull as far off the road as safely possible, shift to park, and set the parking brake. This helps prevent the vehicle from rolling and keeps it stable while you are outside near traffic.

question: If the roadway ahead is filled with heavy smoke, what action should you take?
options: a:Slow, move far right, and stop off the roadway until it is safe to continue.,b:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue slowly.,c:Turn on your high beams and proceed cautiously.,d:Make a U-turn immediately.
note: If smoke or dust makes it hard to see, slow down, move as far to the right as you safely can, and stop completely off the roadway if possible. Turn on your hazard lights so others can see you, and stay stopped until you can see well enough to continue safely. Do not use high beams in smoke and do not keep driving into an area where you cannot see ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Immediately after passing regardless of distance.,b:Only after signaling for at least 10 seconds.,c:When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
note: When you pass on a two‑lane road, you must not move back into your lane until you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed. A good rule is to wait until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and you are at a safe distance ahead. This ensures you do not cut the other driver off and that you have room if you need to slow or stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which factor greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds,b:Low speeds,c:Driving at night only,d:Driving on smooth roads
note: As speed increases, your stopping distance grows rapidly because both your reaction distance and braking distance get longer. Higher speeds also mean much more crash energy, so any collision is likely to be more severe. This is why obeying speed limits and slowing for conditions is critical for safety.

question: Combining alcohol with drugs can have what effect?
options: a:Help cure your illness.,b:Decrease the effects of the drugs and alcohol.,c:Increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.
note: Alcohol and many drugs affect the brain and body in different ways, and when combined they often multiply each other’s effects. This can greatly reduce judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making driving extremely dangerous. You should never drive after using alcohol, drugs, or a combination of both.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Fall farther back than you would behind a passenger vehicle.,b:Follow more closely to reduce wind drag on your car.,c:Drive on the truck's right side and wait to pass.
note: Large trucks need more distance to stop and have big blind spots directly behind them. By following farther back than you would behind a car, you give yourself more time to react and a better view of the road ahead. Never follow a truck closely or linger alongside it in its blind spots.

question: The impairment caused by severe lack of sleep is most similar to which of these?
options: a:The effect that amphetamines have.,b:The effect that alcohol has.,c:The effect that anger has.
note: Fatigue affects your brain and body in ways very similar to alcohol. As you stay awake longer, your reaction time slows, your judgment gets worse, and you may even briefly fall asleep without realizing it (microsleeps). Studies show that being awake for long periods can impair you about as much as having a moderate to high blood alcohol concentration, which is why drowsy driving is so dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a curve, what should you do?
options: a:Activate your turn signal.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Brake hard while in the curve.
note: Before entering a curve, you should slow down to a safe speed while your vehicle is still straight. Braking hard while you are already in the curve can cause you to lose traction and skid. Enter the curve at a reduced speed, then maintain a steady speed through the curve and accelerate gently as you exit if it is safe.

question: Drivers in Nebraska who refuse chemical testing when requested face a license suspension of:
options: a:One year,b:30 days,c:90 days,d:Six months
note: Nebraska’s implied consent law means that by driving, you agree to take a chemical test if an officer lawfully requests it. If you refuse the test, your license can be taken and you face an administrative revocation, commonly for one year on a first refusal. This penalty is separate from any criminal DUI penalties and applies even if you are not later convicted of DUI.

question: When driving in icy or snowy conditions, which technique is most effective at preventing crashes?
options: a:Add extra weight to the vehicle to improve traction.,b:Get off the highway as quickly as possible regardless of route.,c:Reduce speed and increase following distance (avoid abrupt maneuvers).
note: On snow or ice, your tires have much less grip, so sudden steering, braking, or acceleration can easily cause a skid. The safest technique is to slow down well below normal speeds, increase your following distance so you have more time to react, and make all movements—steering, braking, and accelerating—smooth and gradual.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are likely blind or visually impaired.,b:They may be deaf.,c:They may be a police officer.
note: A pedestrian using a white cane (with or without a red tip) or a guide dog is usually blind or visually impaired. You must use extra caution: slow down, be prepared to stop, and always yield the right-of-way. Never honk or try to wave them on; instead, allow them plenty of time and space to cross safely.

question: As you approach an intersection showing a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop before entering the intersection.,c:Only proceed on a green light.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and cross traffic if they are in or entering the intersection.

question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving?
options: a:If you are under the BAC legal limit, you are always safe to drive.,b:Coffee can sober you up quickly.,c:Alcohol impairs judgment.,d:If you can walk a straight line you are safe to drive.
note: Alcohol slows your reactions and impairs judgment, coordination, and decision‑making, even before you reach the legal BAC limit. Because of this, any amount of alcohol can make driving unsafe, and you should never rely on tricks like coffee or balance tests to decide if you can drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your driving lane?
options: a:The driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.,b:You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:You signal your intention for three seconds.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your original lane until you can see the headlights (or front of) the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space and do not cut off the other driver.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what is the correct procedure to return to the road?
options: a:Turn sharply to get back onto the pavement as quickly as possible.,b:Stop immediately and wait for assistance.,c:Reduce speed gradually, then carefully steer back onto the pavement when it is safe.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually while keeping the steering wheel straight. Once your speed is reduced and traffic allows, gently steer back onto the pavement; jerking the wheel sharply can cause you to lose control or skid into another lane.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection has the same requirements as which sign?
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any pedestrians and traffic with the right of way, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit the interstate, when should you begin to reduce speed?
options: a:As you approach the deceleration lane.,b:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,c:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.
note: On interstates, stay at highway speed until you are actually in the deceleration lane. Once in that lane, begin slowing in a smooth, controlled way so you reach the advisory speed by the time you enter the exit ramp. Do not slow early on the main roadway, as that can surprise faster traffic behind you.

question: Never park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
options: a:Five feet,b:10 feet,c:15 feet
note: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is illegal in most U.S. jurisdictions so firefighters can quickly connect hoses in an emergency. Always check for local signs or markings, but if none are present, use the 15‑foot rule as your safe minimum distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you make room for vehicles entering the freeway?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position.,b:Merge into the next lane when possible.,c:Speed up to leave a gap for them.
note: When traffic allows, move over one lane to give entering vehicles space to merge safely. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed slightly so a safe gap opens up for them. Cooperating with merging traffic helps prevent sudden braking and reduces the risk of side‑swipe collisions.

question: When approaching a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, or other assistive device, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed normally.,b:Speed up.,c:Yield the right-of-way.
note: Drivers must always yield the right‑of‑way to pedestrians with guide dogs, white canes, or other assistive devices. Slow down, be prepared to stop, and never honk or rev the engine, as this can confuse or frighten the pedestrian and their service animal.

question: The most common mistake drivers make while backing is:
options: a:Failing to look both ways behind them.,b:Using the mirrors correctly.,c:Backing slowly.
note: The most common backing error is not looking carefully behind you in both directions. Turn your head and look through the rear window, and also check side areas, instead of relying only on mirrors or cameras. Back slowly and be ready to stop if anything enters your path.

question: Within how many days must you apply for a replacement operator's license after changing your name or address?
options: a:90 days.,b:10 days.,c:60 days.
note: When your name or address changes, you must update your driver license record within the required time. Many states, including Washington, require this within 60 days. You must visit a licensing office for a name change, and you may update an address online or in person. Failing to update within the required period can result in outdated records and possible citations.

question: Which of the following is commonly used to direct drivers into the proper turning lanes on some highways?
options: a:Arrows and lane markings painted or signed to indicate lane purposes.,b:Flashing red lights,c:Flashing yellow lights
note: On many roads and highways, arrows and lane-use markings—either painted on the pavement or shown on signs—tell you which lanes are for turning and which are for going straight. These markings help you get into the correct lane well before an intersection so you can turn safely and predictably. Flashing red or yellow lights are traffic control signals, not lane-direction indicators.

question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Traffic laws and regulations.,b:Warning about conditions on or near the road ahead.,c:Directions to cities and towns ahead.
note: Yellow and black diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or changes in road width or surface. Seeing a diamond-shaped warning sign means you should slow down if needed and be prepared for the condition shown on the sign.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle if space allows.,b:Expect the motorcycle to use only half a lane so you can share it.,c:Allow the motorcycle a full lane and do not share lanes.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full traffic lane, just like any other motor vehicle. You must not share a lane side-by-side with a motorcycle. Give motorcycles extra space because they are smaller, less visible, and more vulnerable in a collision, and they may need to change position within the lane to avoid road hazards.

question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, you should:
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,b:Brake suddenly to discourage passing,c:Slow down to create space in front of your vehicle for them to complete the pass.,d:Maintain your speed and ignore them.
note: If another driver wants to pass you, help them do it safely. Slightly reduce your speed to create a larger gap in front of your vehicle so the passing driver has more room to move back into the lane. Do not speed up or brake suddenly, as that can increase the risk of a collision.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to a law enforcement officer?
options: a:Only if you are stopped and cited.,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c:Only if you are involved in a collision.
note: You must carry proof of financial responsibility (insurance) and show it to a law enforcement officer whenever requested after a traffic stop or when you are involved in a collision. It is not limited only to collisions; any lawful stop where the officer asks for it requires you to present proof of insurance.

question: To help prevent hydroplaning in heavy rain, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Decrease your speed.,c:Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
note: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning, you should slow down in heavy rain, especially when water is standing on the road. Lower speed allows your tires to maintain better contact with the pavement. You should not use cruise control in heavy rain because it can prevent you from adjusting speed smoothly and quickly if the vehicle begins to lose traction.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do regarding vehicle lights?
options: a:Drive using your parking lights.,b:Turn on your headlights (low beam).,c:Not turn on any vehicle lights.
note: At dusk, dawn, or on overcast days, you should turn on your low‑beam headlights so other drivers can see you more easily. Parking lights alone are not sufficient for driving and are not a substitute for headlights while the vehicle is moving.

question: What penalties might result from fleeing to avoid arrest?
options: a:The driver can be charged with a misdemeanor or felony offense.,b:The driver could have their operator's license revoked.,c:Both of the above.
note: Attempting to flee or elude law enforcement is a serious offense. Depending on the circumstances, it can be charged as a misdemeanor or a felony, and it can also lead to revocation or suspension of your driver license. Both criminal penalties and licensing consequences are possible.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign indicates:
options: a:A stop requirement.,b:A regulatory instruction.,c:A school zone or school crossing.,d:A railroad crossing.
note: A pentagon‑shaped traffic sign is used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this five‑sided sign, be prepared to slow down, watch for children, and obey any posted school‑zone speed limits.

question: Where is it unlawful to park?
options: a:On a hill.,b:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,c:In a parking lot.
note: Parking on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane is illegal because it blocks pedestrians and cyclists who have the right of way in those areas. Always park only where it is permitted and within the proper distance from the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When your traffic signal is a green arrow.,b:When they are on a road to your left and you arrive at an unmarked intersection at the same time.,c:When entering a street from a garage
note: When you enter a street from a garage, alley, driveway, or private road, you must stop if necessary and yield to all traffic and pedestrians already on the roadway or sidewalk. Drivers on the main road have the right of way in this situation.

question: Is failing to secure children under age six in a federally-approved child safety seat a traffic violation punishable by a $25 fine and one point?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Nebraska law requires children up to age six to be properly secured in a federally‑approved child safety seat. Failing to do so is a traffic violation that can result in a fine and points on the driver’s record, because unrestrained children are at high risk of serious injury in a crash.

question: Which of the following is a common cause of distracted driving?
options: a:Eating,b:Changing a radio station or CD.,c:Talking or texting on a cellular phone.
note: Talking or texting on a cell phone is a major source of distracted driving, but any activity that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving—such as eating or adjusting the radio—can increase your crash risk and should be avoided while the vehicle is moving.

question: In rainy weather, when are turning and stopping most hazardous?
options: a:During the first half hour of rainfall.,b:One half hour after it stops raining.,c:After it has been raining all day.
note: Roads are usually most slippery during the first 10–30 minutes of rainfall. Oil and other residues on the pavement mix with the water and create a slick surface, making turning and stopping especially hazardous at the beginning of a rainstorm.

question: On a green arrow, what must drivers do before proceeding?
options: a:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,b:Proceed without yielding because the arrow gives you the right-of-way.,c:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection before proceeding.
note: A green arrow means you may proceed in the direction of the arrow, but you must first yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians already in the intersection or still clearing it. Once the way is clear, you can go; there is no requirement to wait a set number of seconds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does Nebraska's speed law require of drivers?
options: a:Drive at a speed that is reasonable and safe for current conditions, within posted limits.,b:Always drive at the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,c:Drive five miles per hour over the posted limit to keep traffic flowing.
note: Nebraska’s basic speed law requires you to drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for current conditions, even if that means driving below the posted limit. Factors like rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, or poor visibility may make the posted limit unsafe, and you must slow down accordingly.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Immediately slam on the brakes.,b:Continue driving to the nearest service station.,c:Take your foot off the gas and do not immediately apply the brakes.
note: When a tire blows out, the safest first action is to ease your foot off the accelerator and avoid slamming on the brakes. Grip the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, let it slow down gradually, then gently brake and steer off the road when you have control.

question: If you plan to drink socially, which of these is a safe way to ensure you get home safely?
options: a:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.
note: Planning ahead for a sober ride—such as riding with a friend who has not been drinking, using a taxi, or a rideshare—is the safe way to get home after drinking. Coffee, cold showers, or other “sobering up” tricks do not lower your blood alcohol level or restore safe driving ability.

question: Approaching an intersection controlled by a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until it is safe to proceed, yielding to traffic and pedestrians.,b:Come to a complete stop, then proceed when the way is clear.,c:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution without stopping.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and then proceed only when it is safe. You do not simply slow down; you must fully stop before moving through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a stop sign with no painted crosswalk, where must you stop?
options: a:Before entering the unmarked crosswalk.,b:Inside the unmarked crosswalk.,c:At the stop sign regardless of crosswalk position.
note: At a stop sign, you must stop before entering the crosswalk area, even if it is not painted. An unmarked crosswalk exists at most intersections, and you must stop where the front of your vehicle is before that area so pedestrians and cross traffic are protected. If there is no crosswalk or limit line, stop before entering the intersection.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow in a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light.,b:Drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow at any time.,c:It is never used as a traffic signal.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn is ending. It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light: the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop, entering the intersection only if you cannot safely stop before the stop line or crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you in a no passing zone, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down to allow the passing vehicle to return safely to the travel lane.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Pull off the road.
note: If another driver begins to pass you, your job is to help the pass be completed safely. Stay in your lane and, if needed, slightly reduce your speed so the passing vehicle can return to the lane quickly and safely. Do not speed up or force them to stay in the oncoming lane, and you normally do not pull off the road unless there is an emergency or hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street that has more than one lane going your direction, which lane should you turn into?
options: a:Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.,b:Turn into the middle lane.,c:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.
note: When you turn onto a street with more than one lane going your direction, you must turn into the lane closest to the one you came from. This keeps traffic organized and prevents side‑swipe collisions with vehicles turning from the opposite direction or traveling beside you.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection means:
options: a:Continue at the posted speed without changing behavior.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and wait for green.,d:Yield only to pedestrians
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other traffic already in or close to the intersection and continue only when it is safe.

question: Which combination provides the most effective protection in a crash?
